The Position

The Director, Enterprise Applications is responsible for leading the strategy, lifecycle, and continuous improvement of Gateway’s core enterprise application portfolio. This role oversees a team of product managers and technical specialists accountable for business-critical platforms including Financial Systems, HRIS, Gaming Management Systems (GMS), and other operational and corporate applications.

This leader will act as the primary bridge between the business and technology, ensuring applications deliver measurable value, align with enterprise strategy, and evolve in step with regulatory, operational, and business needs.

Key Responsibilities

Product Strategy & Portfolio Ownership

Own the enterprise product strategy for Gateway’s core application portfolio, including financial, HR, gaming, and operational systems.
Define and maintain product roadmaps aligned with business priorities, operational requirements, and technology standards.
Balance enhancement demand, technical health, regulatory requirements, and vendor roadmaps across multiple platforms.
Establish clear product vision, outcomes, and success measures for each application domain.

Product Delivery & Lifecycle Management

Lead the full product lifecycle from intake and prioritization through delivery, adoption, and optimization.
Partner with Architecture, Security, and IT Operations to ensure scalable, secure, and supportable solutions.
Drive adoption, change readiness, and continuous improvement post?implementation.

Business & Stakeholder Engagement

Serve as a senior point of accountability for business leaders across Finance, Human Resources, Casino Operations, Compliance, and corporate functions.
Facilitate structured intake and prioritization of business demands using transparent, outcome?based decisioning.
Translate business needs into actionable product requirements and trade?off recommendations.
Communicate product roadmap status, risks, and value realization to executives and senior leadership.

Vendor & Platform Management

Oversee strategic vendor relationships for enterprise platforms, including product roadmap alignment and performance management.
Partner with Procurement and Legal on contract negotiations, renewals, and cost optimization.
Ensure vendor solutions meet Gateway’s operational, regulatory, security, and scalability requirements.

People Leadership & Capability Development

Lead, coach, and develop a team of Product Managers across multiple application domains.
Establish consistent product management practices, standards, and governance.
Build strong domain expertise within the team while maintaining enterprise alignment.
Support talent development, succession planning, and performance management.

What You Bring

10+ years of experience in technology, product management, or enterprise application leadership is required.
5+ years in a senior leadership role managing product managers or application portfolios is required.
Proven experience owning and evolving enterprise platforms (Finance, HRIS, ERP, or regulated industry systems) is necessary.
Strong stakeholder management skills with demonstrated executive level communication are required.
Exposure to modern product management practices is required.
Familiarity with Gaming Management Systems (GMS) or other mission critical operational platforms is preferred.
Experience balancing competing priorities across complex, multi business environments is preferred.
Experience in gaming, hospitality, retail, healthcare, or other highly regulated industries is preferred.
Experience operating in a multi site, 24/7 environment is preferred.

Who We Are

Gateway Casinos & Entertainment Limited (“Gateway”) is one of the largest and most diversified gaming and entertainment companies in Canada with 31 gaming properties in British Columbia, Ontario and Alberta. Across its entire portfolio, Gateway currently employs approximately 7,200 people and features approximately 391 table games (including 31 poker tables), 14,288 slots, 81 food and beverage outlets and 564 hotel rooms.

Gateway has been in the business of gaming and entertainment in Canada for more than thirty years and continues to evolve and expand its renowned offerings, including developing casino and restaurant brands. The Gateway to Your Future starts with us.

Gateway celebrates and empowers our team members, who make it all possible. A career at Gateway means working with great people, being recognized for your unique contribution and career advancement opportunities across our 31 locations. Our employees thrive with ongoing training and leadership programs while working in a dynamic and fun environment. See for yourself what it’s like to be on a team that values your vision, skill and energy.

jobs.description:
About The Lacroix Medical Group

A leader in private medicine in Quebec, the Lacroix Medical Group comprises three rapidly growing divisions:

Medical Clinics
Operating Rooms
Biomedical Laboratory

The organization has experienced strong and sustained growth since its founding in 2009 and currently employs nearly 350 people. As part of its strategic plan, the Group aims to accelerate its national and international development.

OUR MISSION

To be the benchmark in private healthcare.

OUR VALUES

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation.

The Mandate

In a context of sustained growth and transformation of its activities, Lacroix Medical Group is seeking a Director of Information Technology who will actively contribute to the organization's technological evolution.

Reporting directly to the President and CEO, the Director of IT plays a strategic role across the entire network. They are responsible for defining, structuring, and developing the IT function to effectively support the organization's operations, growth, and ambitions.

They provide leadership for technology strategy, infrastructure, business systems, cybersecurity, data governance, digital transformation, and artificial intelligence.

He is also responsible for the performance of his team and the organization's technology partner ecosystem. This role is for an experienced, business-oriented, and results-driven IT leader who can combine strategic vision with excellent execution. Your Key Responsibilities IT Strategy and Governance: Define and deploy the IT vision and master plan in line with the strategic, operational, and financial priorities of Groupe médical Lacroix. Advise senior management on investments, risks, and key technological choices.

Performance and Business Continuity

Ensure the performance, robustness, and high availability of the infrastructure and technology platforms essential to the network's medical and administrative activities, including ERP, CRM, DME, LIS, SaaS, and cloud environments.

Digital Transformation, Data, and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and prioritize initiatives to transform the organization through technology, data valorization, automation, and artificial intelligence. Lead major technology projects and ensure their effective integration into operations.

Cybersecurity and Risk Management

Maintain high standards in cybersecurity, information protection, redundancy, and business continuity in an environment where system availability and the protection of medical data are critical.

Leadership and Organizational Performance

Lead and develop a competent, autonomous, and accountable IT team. Establish clear objectives and performance indicators, ensure rigorous budget management, and optimize the contribution of suppliers, consultants, and technology partners.

An Executive Role Close to Operations

At Lacroix Medical Group, technology must meet the realities on the ground.

The IT Director will therefore need to maintain close contact with the various business units and network teams to understand their needs, anticipate challenges, and ensure that technological solutions contribute concretely to operational performance and service quality.

The position consequently requires excellent mobility. The successful candidate will be required to travel regularly throughout the Lacroix network in Quebec to meet with teams, support projects, and remain connected to the operational realities of the various facilities.

This on-the-ground presence is an essential component of the role and not an occasional responsibility.

The mandate expressly includes regular visits to service points.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for an experienced manager with a strong business acumen and excellent technological expertise, recognized for their leadership, judgment, and ability to drive organizational growth.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

A bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science, or a related field;
15 to 20 years of experience in information technology, including a minimum of 5 years in a management role;
Mastery of software architecture and project management;
A solid understanding of multi-site and cloud infrastructures;
Good knowledge of SaaS environments and major business platforms: ERP, CRM, financial systems, telephony, Microsoft 365, and others;
A thorough understanding of the issues cybersecurity, data governance and valorization, and artificial intelligence;
Proven experience in team management and development;
Recognized leadership in transformation and change management;
Ability to prioritize, make decisions, and manage effectively in a complex and evolving environment;
Excellent business acumen and the ability to communicate technological issues to senior management;
Fluency in French and English, both written and spoken;
A valid driver's license, a vehicle, and significant availability for regular travel throughout the network.

The Leader Profile We Are Looking For

Beyond technological expertise, we are looking for someone who stands out for their ability to mobilize, structure, and deliver.

A positive and committed leader with a strong sense of Accountability, the ability to build high-performing teams, manage rigorously, challenge the status quo, and transform technological challenges into concrete solutions for the business. The IT Director must be equally comfortable discussing strategy with senior management and understanding the challenges faced by teams in the field. Conditions and Compensation Lacroix Medical Group offers a competitive total compensation package including: Annual salary of $140,000 to $175,000, depending on experience and expertise; 4 weeks of vacation and 4 paid personal days; RRSP+ program with employer contribution; Cell phone allowance; Lacroix Health Credit; and an annual Lacroix gift card. This benefit can be combined with other benefits for personalized medical services.

Enable safer and more effective digital-health delivery by engaging early, resolving uncertainty, and reducing downstream risk and rework.
Improve the end-to-end partner experience by making CSDS pathways, requirements, decisions, and accountabilities easier to understand and navigate.
Help major health initiatives move from concept to implementation with stronger alignment across technology, clinical needs, operations, security, privacy, procurement, and vendors.

Our client is a highly respected, mission-driven not-for-profit organization dedicated to improving well-being and quality of life in the communities it serves. The organization is seeking a strategic and forward-thinking Vice President, Finance to join its Executive Leadership Team. Reporting to the CEO, the Vice President will provide enterprise-wide leadership across Finance and corporate services, while serving as a trusted advisor to the CEO, Board of Directors, and senior leadership team.

The organization delivers essential services to a large and diverse client base. Behind every service are countless financial, operational, and strategic decisions that turn resources into meaningful impact. As Vice President, Finance, the successful candidate will ensure the financial strength, insight, and discipline needed to advance the mission and support long-term sustainability.

This is an exceptional opportunity for an accomplished finance executive who combines strategic insight with operational leadership and wants to influence meaningful outcomes in a purpose-driven organization. More than a functional leader, the Vice President will be a key enterprise partner, helping shape strategy, support growth, and position the organization for continued success in a complex operating environment.

The Mandate

The mandate extends well beyond traditional financial stewardship. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the VP will help shape organizational strategy, support evidence-based decision-making, and ensure the long-term sustainability of an organization delivering critical services.

In partnership with the CEO, Board, and senior leadership team, the VP will provide strategic financial leadership across planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, treasury, audit, risk management, and compliance. They will ensure financial resources are aligned with organizational priorities while maintaining the discipline and accountability the mission requires.

A key priority will be supporting the organization through a period of growth and change. Using financial insights and performance data, the VP will help evaluate opportunities, inform strategic initiatives, and optimize the deployment of resources in a complex funding and operating environment. Success will require balancing long-term vision with disciplined execution and sound financial management.

Beyond finance, the VP will provide executive oversight of key corporate services, including procurement and facilities, ensuring effective stewardship of organizational resources and infrastructure. The role will also lead efforts to strengthen internal capabilities, foster collaboration across departments, and build a high-performing, engaged team.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to evolve the finance function from a trusted service provider into an even more proactive strategic partner and to enable data-driven decision-making across the organization. Success will be measured not only by financial outcomes, but also by the ability to influence strategy, support growth, and contribute to long-term sustainability and impact.

Leadership and Stewardship

The Vice President, Finance, Corporate Functions and Total Company Expenses is a senior Finance leader responsible for providing strategic financial leadership across the organization's global Corporate Functions, enterprise-wide expense management and significant enterprise initiatives.

The VP serves as a trusted advisor to senior Corporate Function and Finance executives, bringing an independent, enterprise-wide perspective to financial performance, resource allocation, expense management and investment decisions.

Operating across businesses, functions and geographies, the role brings together financial insights to provide senior leadership with a Total Company view of expenses, productivity, investments, risks and opportunities,
while ensuring major enterprise initiatives are appropriately prioritized and deliver measurable business value.

Serve as the senior Finance partner to Corporate Function leaders, providing strategic advice, constructive challenge and decision support.

Translate Corporate Function strategies into clear financial implications, resource requirements and investment choices.

Challenge assumptions and recommend actions to improve financial and operational outcomes.

Lead continued enhancement of Corporate cost allocation methodologies.
Evolve transparency to Business Groups regarding Corporate services and allocated expenses including balancing transparency and precision with the need for allocation methodologies that are practical, understandable and decision useful.

Identify underlying expense trends, emerging pressures and opportunities for management action.
Provide an Enterprise-wide view of expense performance across businesses, functions and geographies.

Partner with Business Group and Corporate Finance teams to establish consistent expense definitions, methodologies and management reporting.
Provide senior executives with a clear narrative explaining what is driving expense performance, and where sustainable opportunities exist.
Lead Finance oversight and insights for enterprise expense-management and productivity programs.
Identify structural opportunities to improve the organization's cost base and operating leverage.
Establish frameworks and metrics for measuring productivity and sustainable expense reduction.
Ensure savings commitments have clearly defined baselines, owners, timing and measurable financial outcomes.
Track execution against enterprise expense commitments and escalate risks or gaps requiring management intervention.
Bring external perspectives and financial-services benchmarks into enterprise expense-management discussions.

Lead the Finance Centre of Excellence for Enterprise Key Initiative governance.

Establish consistent standards for business cases, financial evaluation and approval of significant enterprise investments.
Provide independent Finance challenge of investment assumptions, costs, benefits, execution risks and ongoing operating impacts.
Support executive prioritization of competing investments based on strategic importance, affordability, capacity, risk and expected value.
Establish appropriate financial governance throughout the investment lifecycle, from initial business case through implementation and benefits realization.
Continuously enhance investment-governance frameworks and executive reporting.

You will provide strategic leadership and executive oversight for finance, accounting, business and financial planning, treasury, tax, enterprise risk management, investor relations and procurement, while serving as a trusted advisor to the President & CEO, Board of Directors, and Executive Leadership team.

You will play a critical role in shaping the Corporation’s financial strategy, long-term sustainability, and overall business performance. As the Corporation’s senior financial executive, you will lead the development and execution of financial strategies that support growth across both regulated and competitive businesses, while ensuring sound governance, prudent risk management, disciplined capital allocation, and strong financial stewardship.

The Vice President, Finance & CFO will also play a significant role in evaluating mergers and acquisitions, strategic partnerships, and other significant investment opportunities, providing financial leadership and insight to support the Corporation’s growth strategy.

We are seeking an accomplished and forward-thinking leader with the strategic insight, financial acumen, and executive presence to help guide the Corporation through a period of continued growth and transformation. The successful candidate will be a collaborative and trusted partner who builds strong relationships, influences complex decisions, and leads with integrity, accountability, and a commitment to excellence. Strategic Leadership & Business Performance
:
Partner with the President & CEO, Corporate Development and Executive Leadership team to shape and execute our growth strategy across regulated and competitive businesses.
Provide strategic advice on enterprise strategy, capital deployment, growth, risk and financial implications of major decisions.
Lead financial strategies that support sustainable growth, operational excellence, and long-term value creation.
Align financial plans, resources, funding plans, and performance measures with corporate priorities.
Develop decision frameworks, scenarios, and performance insights that improve the quality and speed of Executive and Board decisions.
Champion accountability, innovation, continuous improvement, and data-driven decision-making.

Growth, M&A, and Competitive Business Development

Lead the financial evaluation of acquisitions, mergers, partnerships, joint ventures, new markets and business opportunities.
Develop transaction and financing structures that balance strategic value, financial returns, tax, regulatory requirements, and overall capital capacity.
Serve as a strategic partner by strengthening business models, pricing, investment governance, performance measures and scalable financial capabilities that support profitable growth.
Co-lead transaction integration and post-investment oversight, including financial systems, controls, cost allocation, synergy tracking and benefits realization, ensuring that approved investments deliver sustainable enterprise value.

Financial Stewardship and Transformation

Provide executive leadership for all finance, accounting and financial planning functions.
Ensure the integrity, accuracy and timeliness of consolidated and operating entity financial reporting, accounting, management information, and external disclosures.
Modernize finance systems, processes, data and analytics to improve efficiency, automation, forecasting accuracy, decision support and the scalability required for business growth and future acquisitions.
Maintain a strong system of internal control, delegated authority, financial policy and assurance that protects the company’s assets and reputation.
Lead enterprise budgeting, forecasting, and performance reporting, providing the President & CEO, Boards and Executive Leadership team with clear, forward-looking insights, and early identification of emerging risks and opportunities.
Support the Corporation’s ESG objectives through financial leadership, performance measurement, reporting, and decision support.

Treasury, Risk Management & Investor Relations:

Lead treasury, financing, liquidity, and capital structure strategies.
Manage effective relationships with municipal shareholders, lenders, rating agencies, and other key financial stakeholders.
Provide executive oversight of the Enterprise Risk Management framework.
Ensure that strategic, financial, transaction and emerging risks are identified, assessed and integrated into capital allocation, business planning, and executive decision making.
Oversee tax planning, compliance, and reporting activities.

Regulatory Affairs:

Advise the President & CEO, Executive Leadership Team and Boards on the financial, strategic and enterprise implications of regulatory policy, emerging requirements and industry developments, identifying opportunities, risks and recommended actions.
Translate regulatory decisions, commitments and emerging policy directions into the financial plans, capital strategy, forecasts, performance measures and risk-management priorities.
Provide executive-level financial leadership for major rate applications, capital funding mechanisms and regulatory initiatives, ensuring that revenue requirements, forecasts, cost allocation, and capital plans are credible, integrated and financially sustainable.
Lead engagement and advocacy with regulators, governments, sector organizations and other stakeholders to advance regulatory frameworks that enable innovation, investments, and improved outcomes for customers and communities.
Partner with General Counsel to integrate and align financial, legal, policy and regulatory perspectives in applications, advocacy, compliance and business development.

Procurement & Supply Chain:

Provide executive leadership and oversight for procurement and supply chain strategy.
Lead the transformation and integration of procurement and supply-chain capabilities, including processes, systems, data, analytics and supplier governance.
Establish procurement policies, controls, authorities, and performance measures and ensure procurement practices support value, transparency, compliance, and prudent risk management.
Promote strategic sourcing, supplier performance management, and continuous improvement.
Partner with business leaders to strengthen commercial decision-making and contract management.

Graduate degree in Commerce, Finance, Business, or related discipline, with a CPA designation.

Strong expertise in financial planning, accounting, treasury, capital management, enterprise risk management, and business performance.

Experience in the energy, utility, or other capital-intensive sector is preferred. Knowledge of the regulated business environment and regulatory processes is an asset.

IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Vice President Finance

Reports: EVP Corporate Services & Chief Financial Officer

Duration: 4 - 6 Months

Location: Toronto

Hybrid (2 - 3 Days on-site)

The Opportunity

Our client is a large, complex and highly respected not-for-profit organization that has experienced significant growth and continues to invest in strengthening the capabilities of its finance function. As part of this evolution, the organization has created an Interim Vice President, Finance role for an initial four-to-six-month mandate. This represents an exciting opportunity for an accomplished senior finance executive to provide experienced leadership to a large team while helping to take the finance function to its next level of maturity.

This is not a traditional "keep the lights on" interim assignment. The organization is looking for a senior finance leader who can quickly understand a complex operating environment, provide stability and leadership through transition, and help increase the value that finance brings to organizational decision-making.

A significant focus will be on strengthening data, analytics, management reporting, budgeting and forecasting, while improving the organization's ability to leverage its existing ERP and financial management tools. The goal is to move beyond simply producing financial information toward providing leaders with stronger insight into performance, trends, risks, opportunities and organizational impact.

The Mandate

Reporting to the CFO & Vice President, Corporate Services, the Interim VP Finance will provide leadership across the finance function while partnering closely with senior executives and operational leaders across the organization.

The successful executive will combine strong financial leadership with a practical understanding of how to modernize finance within a large, operationally complex and mission-driven environment.

Key priorities will include:
Lead and engage a large finance team through a period of transition, providing visible leadership, clarity, coaching and direction while maintaining operational continuity.
Assess the current finance operating model, capabilities, processes and priorities, identifying opportunities to enhance the effectiveness and value of the function.
Lead a complex organization-wide budgeting and forecasting process, ensuring appropriate financial discipline while improving the quality of planning, assumptions and scenario analysis.
Strengthen management reporting and financial analytics, ensuring senior leaders have more timely, relevant and actionable information to support decision-making.
Improve the organization's approach to financial metrics, KPIs and performance reporting, creating greater visibility into organizational performance and impact.
Help finance move beyond historical reporting toward a more forward-looking, insight-driven business partnership model.
Maximize the value being generated from the organization's ERP, reporting tools and financial data, identifying opportunities to improve processes, reporting capabilities and management insight without creating unnecessary complexity.
Work closely with operational and functional leaders to better understand their information requirements and strengthen finance's ability to support business decisions.
Review existing financial processes and controls and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, consistency, scalability and accountability.
Provide strategic financial advice and support to the CFO & Vice President, Corporate Services and broader executive leadership team.
Ensure the organization continues to maintain strong financial stewardship, controls, governance and accountability throughout the period of transition.
Build capability within the finance team through coaching, knowledge transfer and the development of stronger analytical and business-partnering skills.
What Success Looks Like
At the conclusion of the assignment, the organization should have:
A stable, engaged and well-led finance team positioned for the next stage of the organization's growth.
A clearer understanding of the capabilities, structure and priorities required within finance going forward.
A more robust and effective budgeting and forecasting process.
Significantly improved management reporting and financial insight.
More meaningful financial and operational metrics supporting executive decision-making.
Greater value being generated from existing ERP, reporting and data capabilities.
Stronger relationships between finance and operational leadership.
A finance function increasingly viewed as a strategic partner to the organization rather than simply a reporting and transactional function.
Clear recommendations for the continued modernization and evolution of finance beyond the interim mandate.

Ideal Background

The successful candidate will be a seasoned, CPA-designated finance executive who has led sizeable finance functions within large, complex organizations.

Ideally, they will bring:
CPA designation is mandatory.
Significant progressive finance leadership experience, ideally including VP Finance, CFO, Deputy CFO or similarly senior responsibilities.
Experience working within a large, complex not-for-profit, healthcare, broader public sector, association, social services or other mission-driven organization.
Demonstrated experience operating in an organization of 1,500+ employees or an environment of comparable scale and complexity.
Experience leading finance teams of approximately 15–20+ professionals, including managers and senior finance professionals.
Strong experience leading teams through transition, growth, modernization or organizational change.
Deep expertise in budgeting, forecasting, financial planning and management reporting within a complex organization.
A track record of improving financial analytics, dashboards, KPIs and decision-support capabilities.
Experience maximizing and improving the use of ERP systems and financial reporting tools, with the ability to focus on business outcomes rather than technology for technology's sake.
Strong understanding of financial governance, controls, reporting and stewardship within environments with multiple stakeholders and competing priorities.
Demonstrated ability to develop finance teams and build stronger FP&A, analytical and business-partnering capability.
The ability to operate comfortably at both a strategic and hands-on level, moving from executive discussions into the detail when required.
Strong communication and stakeholder-management capabilities, with the credibility to influence senior executives and operational leaders across a complex organization.
A pragmatic, collaborative and confident leadership style, with the ability to quickly establish trust and bring calm, experienced leadership during a period of change.
The Leadership Profile
This assignment will particularly suit an executive who has "seen the movie before."
The organization is not looking for someone simply to administer an established finance function. It needs an experienced finance leader who can step into a complex environment, quickly determine what matters, lead a substantial team confidently through transition and identify practical opportunities to make finance better.
The successful executive will bring a combination of financial stewardship, operational leadership, transformation experience and commercial curiosity. They will understand that great
finance organizations do more than report the numbers. They provide the analysis, insight and constructive challenge that allows leaders to make better decisions.
For the right executive, this is an opportunity to make a tangible impact within a large, mission-driven organization and leave the finance function stronger, more insightful and better equipped to support the organization's continued growth.

Lead and support an established, high-performing FP&A team through a period of leadership transition.
Own and drive a critical organization-wide budgeting and forecasting process, ensuring key milestones, deliverables and timelines are achieved.

Coach and support the FP&A team, maintaining engagement, accountability and confidence during the transition.

Technology, Data & Insights

Advanced Excel-based financial modelling and analysis.
Power BI dashboards, analytics and management reporting.
Budgeting and forecasting systems.
ERP and financial reporting platforms.
Multi-entity financial reporting and consolidation.
Scenario modelling and sensitivity analysis.
Systems implementation, adoption and optimization.
Translating complex financial data into meaningful management insight.
The individual does not need to be a technology specialist. They do, however, need to understand how technology, data and financial modelling can be used to make FP&A faster, more insightful and more valuable to organizational decision makers.

What Success Looks Like

At the conclusion of the three-month assignment, the organization should have:
Successfully navigated a critical budgeting cycle.
Maintained stability, engagement and performance within an already strong FP&A team.
Embedded and optimized the organization's new budgeting process and supporting technology.
Increased confidence in budgeting, forecasting and management reporting.
Improved financial modelling and scenario-planning capabilities.
Better utilization of Excel, Power BI and existing financial reporting tools.
Clearer consolidated reporting across a complex, multi-entity environment.
Stronger financial insight available to senior leadership to support decision-making.
A well-positioned FP&A function ready for the next stage of its development.

Ideal Background

The ideal candidate will bring:

Significant experience leading Financial Planning & Analysis within a large, complex not-for-profit organization.
Previous experience within the not-for-profit, healthcare, broader public sector, association, social services or another complex mission-driven environment.
A recognized accounting designation, MBA in Finance or equivalent senior-level financial qualification and experience.
Demonstrated experience leading and developing established finance and FP&A teams.
Strong expertise in complex budgeting, forecasting and long-range financial planning.
Advanced Excel financial modelling capabilities.
Strong experience with Power BI and other management-reporting and visualization tools.
Experience working with ERP, budgeting and financial reporting platforms, including system implementation, adoption or optimization.
Experience with multi-entity environments and consolidated financial reporting is highly desirable.
Strong analytical capability with the ability to move beyond reporting numbers to explaining what they mean and what leadership should do about them.
Experience working with senior executives and operational leaders in organizations with multiple stakeholders, competing priorities and significant complexity.

This is an assignment for someone who can quickly establish credibility, support a strong team, roll up their sleeves when required and confidently navigate senior stakeholders through a complex budgeting process.

Above all, they will know how to use FP&A for what it should ultimately be: not simply producing budgets and reports, but giving leaders the financial insight, foresight and confidence to make better decisions.

As a leader who helped shape the industry, Draganfly’s focus is on the sale of drone products and services, contract engineering & custom integration product development, and health monitoring products and services.

Additional information on our expertise, projects, and culture can be found at https://draganfly.com/

We are looking for a strategic, highly hands-on, execution-focused Director, Enterprise Applications to lead the strategy, transformation, delivery and operation of Draganfly’s core business platforms and processes, including ERP and procurement systems. This is a working leadership role, not a purely strategic or people-management position. The successful candidate will be expected to personally analyze business processes, configure and optimize systems, troubleshoot issues, work with data and integrations, lead implementations, test solutions, and drive projects through completion. While this role will work closely with vendors, consultants and internal teams, the Director must be comfortable rolling up their sleeves and doing the work directly rather than primarily delegating execution to others.

As Draganfly grows across Canada, the US and internationally, this leader will modernize and standardize our application landscape across Draganfly Inc., Draganfly Innovations Inc., Draganfly Innovations USA, Draganfly Defense, USA, and Candrone. The role requires a leader who can partner with senior executives, work with colleagues within each department, drive execution at scale, and be part of a high-performing team.

This is a remote role, but the successful candidate will need to be willing to travel.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy & Transformation

Define and execute the enterprise applications strategy and multi-year roadmap across ERP, finance, procurement and related corporate systems.

Lead transformation initiatives that standardize and simplify business processes, modernize legacy tools and consolidate platforms in the cloud.

Align related application roadmaps with Draganfly’s business priorities, growth plans and multi-entity operating structure.

Delivery & Value

Own delivery of enterprise initiatives from initial requirements through hands-on configuration, testing, implementation and post-launch support.

Define and track measurable outcomes such as facilitating with operations a faster financial close, with finance chart of account updates, new subsidiary uploads, greater AP/AR automation and fewer manual, spreadsheet-dependent processes.

Ensure finance platforms support Record-to-Report (R2R) and multi-entity consolidation and reporting, and that HR systems support the Hire-to-Retire (H2R) lifecycle, including payroll, benefits and talent management.

Ensure the platforms support Order-to-Cash (O2C), Procure-to-Pay (P2P), contract visibility and supplier management.

Process Standardization

Partner with Finance, HR, Legal, Procurement, Sales and Supply Chain leaders to define and implement best-practice processes across all entities.

Drive automation and deliver improvements in cycle times, data quality and reporting transparency.

Act as a primary point of contact for process optimization, supporting change management and driving consistency in process standardization.

Architecture & Integration

Define the target-state application architecture and integration patterns across the ERP and dependent data platforms.

Ensure systems are secure, auditable and integrated through scalable APIs and middleware, and guide build-versus-buy decisions.

Governance, Risk & Compliance

Ensure enterprise platforms meet public company financial controls and audit requirements (Canada and US), including COSO Framework, SOX404b protocols, as well as data governance and privacy obligations.

Collaborate closely with IT and Security to ensure compliance with security standards and business continuity planning.

Support export control and trade compliance requirements as required through appropriate system controls, data, and reporting.

Vendor Management

Manage platform vendors, implementation partners and consultants, holding them accountable for delivery performance, cost, and quality.

Leadership

Working manager that can also build and lead a high-performing enterprise applications team, with clear operating models for project delivery, production support and release and change management.

Foster a culture of accountability, cross-functional collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Other duties as assigned.

Who are you really?

A hands-on builder who rolls up their sleeves to configure systems, troubleshoot issues and see projects through to completion, rather than primarily delegating execution

A strategic thinker who can set a multi-year enterprise applications roadmap and standardize processes across multiple entities as Draganfly grows

A strong communicator with executive presence who can translate technical concepts for technical and non-technical audiences and influence the CFO and leaders across Finance, HR, Legal and Operations

Self-driven and dependable, able to manage multiple initiatives independently in a fast-paced, high-growth environment

A vendor and partner manager who holds implementation partners and consultants accountable for delivery, cost and quality

A collaborative team builder who fosters accountability and continuous improvement, and is comfortable working across ERP, HRIS and procurement platforms such as Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central

You bring a positive, solutions-oriented mindset, thrive in a role where attention to detail and controls matter, and are willing to travel as needed.

Qualifications

Education & Experience

10+ years in enterprise applications, IT or digital transformation, including 5+ years in leadership roles leading cross-functional teams.

Proven success leading ERP and finance system implementations or transformations, ideally in a multi-entity environment.

Deep experience with ERP platforms (Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central), HRIS (e.g. Rippling, Workday) and CLM/procurement platforms.

Track record of delivering complex, multi-year programs with measurable business outcomes.

Strong understanding of finance systems, including general ledger, fixed assets, revenue, consolidation, and reporting.

Strong working knowledge of R2R, P2P, O2C, and H2R processes.

Experience with public company financial controls and audit requirements (Canada and US), awareness of export control and trade compliance, and efficient companywide supply chain management.

Strong understanding of enterprise integration (APIs, middleware), cloud platforms, and data governance principles.

Ability to translate complex business needs into scalable, sustainable technology solutions.

Strong executive presence and the ability to influence the CFO and leaders across HR, Legal, Operations and the wider

Experience building and scaling teams and aligning stakeholders across competing priorities.

Ability and willingness to personally troubleshoot systems, configure workflows, work with data, participate in testing and resolve implementation and production issues. business.

Ability to travel

Specializations/Nice to Haves

Experience in manufacturing, aerospace, defence or technology hardware.

Experience modernizing legacy systems into scalable cloud platforms.

Experience with HubSpot CRM and its integration with ERP.

Familiarity with AI-enabled capabilities (e.g. Microsoft Copilot, intelligent automation).

MBA or equivalent.

Compensation Package

Equity / Stock Options: Participation in the company’s stock option plan, providing long‑term ownership and alignment with company growth.

Comprehensive medical and dental benefits, including a Health Spending Account (HSA).

Matching RRSP program to support long‑term financial planning.

Generous time‑off program, including vacation, wellness days, and the full week off between Christmas and New Year’s.

Professional development support, including assistance toward obtaining your FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate or equivalent training required for operational roles.

Why Join Us

At Draganfly Innovations, you’ll join a collaborative team that values innovation, curiosity, and continuous improvement. We’re in an exciting growth phase, scaling our technologies, product lines, and teams as we continue to shape the future of UAV innovation. Joining us now means becoming part of a company with deep roots in the industry - and bold ambitions for what comes next.

You’ll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact, work on diverse and cutting‑edge projects, and grow your skills alongside passionate experts. We offer competitive compensation, strong benefits, and a supportive environment where your contributions truly matter. Here, you won’t just join a company - you’ll help build what comes next.

Job Description:

The Vice President, Finance, Corporate Functions and Total Company Expenses is a senior Finance leader responsible for providing strategic financial leadership across the organization's global Corporate Functions, enterprise-wide expense management and significant enterprise initiatives.

The VP serves as a trusted advisor to senior Corporate Function and Finance executives, bringing an independent, enterprise-wide perspective to financial performance, resource allocation, expense management and investment decisions.

Operating across businesses, functions and geographies, the role brings together financial insights to provide senior leadership with a Total Company view of expenses, productivity, investments, risks and opportunities,
while ensuring major enterprise initiatives are appropriately prioritized and deliver measurable business value.

Key Role Accountabilities

Corporate Segment

Serve as the senior Finance partner to Corporate Function leaders, providing strategic advice, constructive challenge and decision support.
Lead planning, forecasting, reporting and performance management across Corporate Functions.
Translate Corporate Function strategies into clear financial implications, resource requirements and investment choices.
Provide forward-looking insights on financial performance, emerging risks, opportunities and structural cost drivers.
Challenge assumptions and recommend actions to improve financial and operational outcomes.
Maintain view of Corporate Function costs and the underlying services and capabilities driving those costs.
Lead continued enhancement of Corporate cost allocation methodologies.
Evolve transparency to Business Groups regarding Corporate services and allocated expenses including balancing transparency and precision with the need for allocation methodologies that are practical, understandable and decision useful.
Partner with Business Group Finance leaders to understand cost drivers, forecast allocations and identify optimization opportunities.
Partner with Capital, Investment teams and tax for Corporate segment results, forecasts and plan

Lead the consolidation, analysis and executive reporting of Total Company expenses.

Identify underlying expense trends, emerging pressures and opportunities for management action.
Provide an Enterprise-wide view of expense performance across businesses, functions and geographies.
Develop forward-looking insights regarding the organization's expense trajectory and key financial sensitivities.
Partner with Business Group and Corporate Finance teams to establish consistent expense definitions, methodologies and management reporting.
Provide senior executives with a clear narrative explaining what is driving expense performance, and where sustainable opportunities exist.
Lead Finance oversight and insights for enterprise expense-management and productivity programs.
Identify structural opportunities to improve the organization's cost base and operating leverage.
Establish frameworks and metrics for measuring productivity and sustainable expense reduction.
Ensure savings commitments have clearly defined baselines, owners, timing and measurable financial outcomes.
Track execution against enterprise expense commitments and escalate risks or gaps requiring management intervention.
Bring external perspectives and financial-services benchmarks into enterprise expense-management discussions.

Lead the Finance Centre of Excellence for Enterprise Key Initiative governance.

Establish consistent standards for business cases, financial evaluation and approval of significant enterprise investments.
Provide independent Finance challenge of investment assumptions, costs, benefits, execution risks and ongoing operating impacts.
Support executive prioritization of competing investments based on strategic importance, affordability, capacity, risk and expected value.
Establish appropriate financial governance throughout the investment lifecycle, from initial business case through implementation and benefits realization.
Continuously enhance investment-governance frameworks and executive reporting.
As the team and company grow, the responsibilities of this position may expand to adapt to changing organizational goals.

IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Director Financial Planning and Analysis

Reports: Vice President Finance

Duration: 3 Months

Location: Toronto

Hybrid Work (2 – 3 Days onsite)

The Opportunity

This is an exciting opportunity for an accomplished FP&A leader to step into a large, complex Canadian not-for-profit organization at a critical point in its annual financial planning cycle.

Following a recent departure, the organization requires an experienced Interim Director of Financial Planning & Analysis to provide immediate leadership to an established, high-performing team and successfully steer the organization through a complex and evolving budgeting process.

This is not a "blow it up and rebuild it" assignment. The foundations are strong, the team is capable, and significant work is already underway. The mandate is about bringing experienced, steady leadership, maintaining momentum and getting the very best from the people, processes, technology and financial information already in place.

A major focus will be optimizing the use of Excel, and existing financial reporting tools to provide stronger modelling, analysis and insight throughout the budgeting process. The successful interim will help ensure that a new budgeting approach and supporting technology are effectively embedded while giving senior leadership confidence in the integrity, quality and usefulness of the organization's financial information.

The Mandate

The Interim Director, Financial Planning & Analysis will take immediate leadership of the FP&A function during a particularly important period for the organization.
Key priorities will include:
Lead and support an established, high-performing FP&A team through a period of leadership transition.
Own and drive a critical organization-wide budgeting and forecasting process, ensuring key milestones, deliverables and timelines are achieved.
Provide strong financial leadership as the organization works through a new budgeting process and associated technology.
Optimize the use of Excel, Power BI and existing reporting platforms to strengthen financial modelling, analysis, reporting and decision support.
Develop and enhance sophisticated financial models to support budgeting, forecasting, scenario planning and organizational decision-making.
Ensure senior executives and operational leaders receive clear, timely and actionable financial information throughout the budgeting cycle.
Support business leaders in understanding budgets, assumptions, variances, risks and financial implications across their respective areas.
Bring together financial information across multiple entities and business areas, ensuring accurate and meaningful consolidated reporting.
Identify practical opportunities to improve the use of existing systems and reporting capabilities without introducing unnecessary disruption or change.
Maintain strong financial discipline and consistency across the budgeting and forecasting process.
Partner closely with senior finance leadership and other organizational stakeholders, providing informed analysis, constructive challenge and practical financial advice.
Coach and support the FP&A team, maintaining engagement, accountability and confidence during the transition.

Technology, Data & Insights

A key component of this assignment will be helping the organization get more value from its existing technology and financial information.

The successful interim will be comfortable working in a technology-enabled finance environment and will bring particular strength in:

Advanced Excel-based financial modelling and analysis.
Power BI dashboards, analytics and management reporting.
Budgeting and forecasting systems.
ERP and financial reporting platforms.
Multi-entity financial reporting and consolidation.
Scenario modelling and sensitivity analysis.
Systems implementation, adoption and optimization.
Translating complex financial data into meaningful management insight.
The individual does not need to be a technology specialist. They do, however, need to understand how technology, data and financial modelling can be used to make FP&A faster, more insightful and more valuable to organizational decision makers.

What Success Looks Like

At the conclusion of the three-month assignment, the organization should have:
Successfully navigated a critical budgeting cycle.
Maintained stability, engagement and performance within an already strong FP&A team.
Embedded and optimized the organization's new budgeting process and supporting technology.
Increased confidence in budgeting, forecasting and management reporting.
Improved financial modelling and scenario-planning capabilities.
Better utilization of Excel, Power BI and existing financial reporting tools.
Clearer consolidated reporting across a complex, multi-entity environment.
Stronger financial insight available to senior leadership to support decision-making.
A well-positioned FP&A function ready for the next stage of its development.

Ideal Background

The ideal candidate will bring:

Significant experience leading Financial Planning & Analysis within a large, complex not-for-profit organization.
Previous experience within the not-for-profit, healthcare, broader public sector, association, social services or another complex mission-driven environment.
A recognized accounting designation, MBA in Finance or equivalent senior-level financial qualification and experience.
Demonstrated experience leading and developing established finance and FP&A teams.
Strong expertise in complex budgeting, forecasting and long-range financial planning.
Advanced Excel financial modelling capabilities.
Strong experience with Power BI and other management-reporting and visualization tools.
Experience working with ERP, budgeting and financial reporting platforms, including system implementation, adoption or optimization.
Experience with multi-entity environments and consolidated financial reporting is highly desirable.
Strong analytical capability with the ability to move beyond reporting numbers to explaining what they mean and what leadership should do about them.
Experience working with senior executives and operational leaders in organizations with multiple stakeholders, competing priorities and significant complexity.

This is an assignment for someone who can quickly establish credibility, support a strong team, roll up their sleeves when required and confidently navigate senior stakeholders through a complex budgeting process.

Above all, they will know how to use FP&A for what it should ultimately be: not simply producing budgets and reports, but giving leaders the financial insight, foresight and confidence to make better decisions.

About Draganfly

Draganfly Inc. (the “Company”) has been a recognized technology leader within the commercial UAV space for over two decades. We helped establish the commercial market & adoption of multi-rotor helicopters for public safety, agriculture, aerial imaging, & more. As a leader who helped shape the industry, Draganfly’s focus is on the sale of drone products and services, contract engineering & custom integration product development, and health monitoring products and services.

Additional information on our expertise, projects, and culture can be found at https://draganfly.com/

We are looking for a strategic, highly hands-on, execution-focused Director, Enterprise Applications to lead the strategy, transformation, delivery and operation of Draganfly’s core business platforms and processes, including ERP and procurement systems. This is a working leadership role, not a purely strategic or people-management position. The successful candidate will be expected to personally analyze business processes, configure and optimize systems, troubleshoot issues, work with data and integrations, lead implementations, test solutions, and drive projects through completion. While this role will work closely with vendors, consultants and internal teams, the Director must be comfortable rolling up their sleeves and doing the work directly rather than primarily delegating execution to others.

As Draganfly grows across Canada, the US and internationally, this leader will modernize and standardize our application landscape across Draganfly Inc., Draganfly Innovations Inc., Draganfly Innovations USA, Draganfly Defense, USA, and Candrone. The role requires a leader who can partner with senior executives, work with colleagues within each department, drive execution at scale, and be part of a high-performing team.

This is a remote role, but the successful candidate will need to be willing to travel.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy & Transformation

Define and execute the enterprise applications strategy and multi-year roadmap across ERP, finance, procurement and related corporate systems.

Lead transformation initiatives that standardize and simplify business processes, modernize legacy tools and consolidate platforms in the cloud.

Align related application roadmaps with Draganfly’s business priorities, growth plans and multi-entity operating structure.

Delivery & Value

Own delivery of enterprise initiatives from initial requirements through hands-on configuration, testing, implementation and post-launch support.

Define and track measurable outcomes such as facilitating with operations a faster financial close, with finance chart of account updates, new subsidiary uploads, greater AP/AR automation and fewer manual, spreadsheet-dependent processes.

Platform Leadership

Hands on execution of Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central and procurement across their full lifecycle, from evaluation and selection of new platforms to ongoing optimization of existing platforms.

Work directly in the systems and with end users to identify issues, determine root causes and implement practical solutions.

Ensure finance platforms support Record-to-Report (R2R) and multi-entity consolidation and reporting, and that HR systems support the Hire-to-Retire (H2R) lifecycle, including payroll, benefits and talent management.

Ensure the platforms support Order-to-Cash (O2C), Procure-to-Pay (P2P), contract visibility and supplier management.

Process Standardization

Partner with Finance, HR, Legal, Procurement, Sales and Supply Chain leaders to define and implement best-practice processes across all entities.

Drive automation and deliver improvements in cycle times, data quality and reporting transparency.

Act as a primary point of contact for process optimization, supporting change management and driving consistency in process standardization.

Architecture & Integration

Define the target-state application architecture and integration patterns across the ERP and dependent data platforms.

Ensure systems are secure, auditable and integrated through scalable APIs and middleware, and guide build-versus-buy decisions.

Governance, Risk & Compliance

Ensure enterprise platforms meet public company financial controls and audit requirements (Canada and US), including COSO Framework, SOX404b protocols, as well as data governance and privacy obligations.

Collaborate closely with IT and Security to ensure compliance with security standards and business continuity planning.

Support export control and trade compliance requirements as required through appropriate system controls, data, and reporting.

Vendor Management

Manage platform vendors, implementation partners and consultants, holding them accountable for delivery performance, cost, and quality.

Leadership

Working manager that can also build and lead a high-performing enterprise applications team, with clear operating models for project delivery, production support and release and change management.

Foster a culture of accountability, cross-functional collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Other duties as assigned.

Who are you really?

A hands-on builder who rolls up their sleeves to configure systems, troubleshoot issues and see projects through to completion, rather than primarily delegating execution

A strategic thinker who can set a multi-year enterprise applications roadmap and standardize processes across multiple entities as Draganfly grows

A strong communicator with executive presence who can translate technical concepts for technical and non-technical audiences and influence the CFO and leaders across Finance, HR, Legal and Operations

Self-driven and dependable, able to manage multiple initiatives independently in a fast-paced, high-growth environment

A vendor and partner manager who holds implementation partners and consultants accountable for delivery, cost and quality

A collaborative team builder who fosters accountability and continuous improvement, and is comfortable working across ERP, HRIS and procurement platforms such as Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central

You bring a positive, solutions-oriented mindset, thrive in a role where attention to detail and controls matter, and are willing to travel as needed.

Qualifications

Education & Experience

10+ years in enterprise applications, IT or digital transformation, including 5+ years in leadership roles leading cross-functional teams.

Proven success leading ERP and finance system implementations or transformations, ideally in a multi-entity environment.

Deep experience with ERP platforms (Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central), HRIS (e.g. Rippling, Workday) and CLM/procurement platforms.

Track record of delivering complex, multi-year programs with measurable business outcomes.

Strong understanding of finance systems, including general ledger, fixed assets, revenue, consolidation, and reporting.

Strong working knowledge of R2R, P2P, O2C, and H2R processes.

Experience with public company financial controls and audit requirements (Canada and US), awareness of export control and trade compliance, and efficient companywide supply chain management.

Strong understanding of enterprise integration (APIs, middleware), cloud platforms, and data governance principles.

Ability to translate complex business needs into scalable, sustainable technology solutions.

Strong executive presence and the ability to influence the CFO and leaders across HR, Legal, Operations and the wider

Experience building and scaling teams and aligning stakeholders across competing priorities.

Ability and willingness to personally troubleshoot systems, configure workflows, work with data, participate in testing and resolve implementation and production issues. business.

Ability to travel

Specializations/Nice to Haves

Experience in manufacturing, aerospace, defence or technology hardware.

Experience modernizing legacy systems into scalable cloud platforms.

Experience with HubSpot CRM and its integration with ERP.

Familiarity with AI-enabled capabilities (e.g. Microsoft Copilot, intelligent automation).

MBA or equivalent.

Compensation Package

Equity / Stock Options: Participation in the company’s stock option plan, providing long‑term ownership and alignment with company growth.

Comprehensive medical and dental benefits, including a Health Spending Account (HSA).

Matching RRSP program to support long‑term financial planning.

Generous time‑off program, including vacation, wellness days, and the full week off between Christmas and New Year’s.

Professional development support, including assistance toward obtaining your FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate or equivalent training required for operational roles.

Why Join Us

At Draganfly Innovations, you’ll join a collaborative team that values innovation, curiosity, and continuous improvement. We’re in an exciting growth phase, scaling our technologies, product lines, and teams as we continue to shape the future of UAV innovation. Joining us now means becoming part of a company with deep roots in the industry - and bold ambitions for what comes next.

We offer competitive compensation, strong benefits, and a supportive environment where your contributions truly matter. Here, you won’t just join a company - you’ll help build what comes next.

comprises three rapidly growing divisions:

Medical Clinics

OUR MISSION

To be the benchmark in private healthcare.

OUR VALUES

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation

Mandate

Reporting to the Director of Marketing, the Digital Performance Manager
plays a key role in the growth, reach, and success of the Lacroix Medical Group.

Passionate about digital marketing, data, and innovation, this individual leverages their expertise to develop high-performing strategies that generate a tangible impact on our business objectives. Their daily challenge: transforming data into opportunities, strategies into results, and ideas into measurable actions. In a dynamic environment encompassing multiple clinics, services, and business lines, the successful candidate will lead the organization's overall digital performance. They will develop, deploy, measure, and optimize digital media campaigns to increase our visibility, generate business opportunities, and maximize the return on our marketing investments. A true strategic partner to internal teams, this proactive individual will work closely with various stakeholders to understand their challenges, identify the best growth opportunities, and recommend innovative, results-oriented solutions. Curious, analytical, and always on the lookout for new trends, the Digital Performance Manager enjoys experimenting, innovating, and pushing boundaries. Whether through campaign optimization, advanced data analytics, artificial intelligence, geolocation, or new approaches to digital marketing, this individual helps maintain the Lacroix Medical Group's position among the most innovative organizations in its sector.
